_meta: One query's pre-softmax attention scores over a batch's key positions, where the last position is padding, used to show why padding must be masked in the ATTENTION (its key scores set to negative infinity before the softmax) and not only in the loss: without the mask, a real token's attention distribution spreads weight onto the pad position and mixes the pad embedding's value into the token's output, corrupting its representation. To batch sequences of different lengths together, shorter sequences are padded to the batch's maximum length with a filler token. Those pad positions are not real content, but they still have embeddings, and those embeddings still produce key vectors and therefore attention scores -- often perfectly ordinary-looking scores. If nothing masks them, the softmax over a query's scores includes the pad positions, so some of the query's attention weight lands on padding and the corresponding pad values are averaged into the query's output. The token's representation is now contaminated by meaningless filler, and every downstream layer inherits the contamination. This is separate from masking padding out of the loss (which stops filler from diluting the training signal); attention masking stops filler from corrupting the forward-pass representations. The fix is to set the pad positions' scores to negative infinity before the softmax, so the softmax assigns them exactly zero weight and the attention is taken only over the real tokens, whose weights are renormalized to sum to one. scores is the query's raw score for each key position; is_pad marks which positions are padding. These are the fixture; the softmax attention weights with and without the pad mask, and the weight that leaks onto padding, are computed.
